checks.label: A horizontal line drawn on the graph cuts it more than once, so two different inputs have yielded the same output and the function is many-to-one: on the square the level line meets the U twice at every level above its bottom, at two different inputs that both give that level, and at 4 they are −2 and 2

On the line, the cube, the one-over and the root the level line meets the curve at most once at every level it can be dragged to, each meeting's input giving that level, and the one-over is never cut at 0
The root of a number from 0 to 1 is larger, √0.5 = 0.707, so 50% of the pressure difference is 71% of the flow: the root's table reads 0.707 for 0.5, and the flow rule turns 50% into 71%

The pressure difference goes with the square of the flow, so the flow is found from its square root: every flow on the graph, squared as a fraction of full, gives back its pressure difference, and 25% of the difference reads 50% flow
Power lost depends upon the square of the current: on the 1 Ω run twice the current loses four times the power, 3 A loses 9 W and 6 A 36 W, and the graph reads 36 W at 6 A
The generalised propeller law makes engine load proportional to the cube of propeller speed: half speed carries 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.125 of full load, 12.5%, and the graph reads 12.5% at 50% speed

Plotting a gas's pressure against its volume gives a hyperbola: the three points keep pressure × volume the same, each halving of the volume doubles the pressure, and the right answer draws the one-over curve through all three

Instruments convert with the linear equation y = mx + b, a straight line: table A, 1, 3, 5, 7, rises by 2 at every step, the line y = x by 1 at every step, and the right answer draws A's three equal rises of 2

Every worked number is right: y = x gives 1, 2, 3 for 1, 2, 3; the square gives 9 for −3 and 3, and 0, 1, 4, 9 rise by 1, 3, 5; the 1 Ω run loses 9 W at 3 A and 36 W at 6 A, against 18 W and 81 W; the cube gives −8 and 8 for −2 and 2, and 0.125 for 0.5; half speed is 12.5% of full load, against 50% and 25%; the one-over gives 0.5 and 0.25 for 2 and 4; 12 V draws 4 A through 3 Ω and 2 A through 6 Ω, against 8 A and 1 A; the root gives 1, 2, 3 for 1, 4, 9; 25% of the difference gives 50% flow, against 25% and 6.25%; the level line at 4 cuts the square at −2 and 2; 9 W comes from −3 A and 3 A, against 4.5 A; and 12 V through 2, 4 and 8 Ω draws 6, 3 and 1.5 A
Before Check a puzzle draws no answer; a right answer draws its reading and nothing in red, and each wrong answer draws its own slip in red, with the slip's value where it names one

Every dot sits on its curve at its place, every value written on an axis is that dot's own reading, and every filled table row is its rule's output: on each demonstration, every place Dan can drag to, and every puzzle answer

The table fills as the point rides: in each demonstration a row fills only once the pointer has reached its input, every input the pointer passes is filled by the end, and at least one row is left for Dan to fill
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its 3.4 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
